A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HiGarment/FS2RG study. All text, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v2's supplementary Sections 7–10. Relocated material can be matched reliably; v1 contains no separate appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation experiments, quantitative comparisons, human/MLLM evaluations and component ablations in Section 5 and Tables 2–4.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds a dataset ablation, attention visualizations and illustrated failure cases.

M1.justification: The fabric-retrieval/Q-Former enhancement, harmonized cross-attention, diffusion backbone and loss remain unchanged. MSE is renamed MMSE. Expanded dictionary-normalization and fallback descriptions clarify the existing procedure without establishing an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: V2 adds fine-tuning described as using VITON-HD and reports tests with fabric names absent from the database. V1 only reports experiments using MMDGarment. The exact VITON variant is inconsistently cited, but additional dataset coverage is clear. Fabric-unspecified prompts already appear in v1's qualitative examples.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain IP-Adapter, Uni-ControlNet, Versatile Diffusion, DEADiff and SSR-Encoder. Human/MLLM comparisons retain IP-Adapter and DEADiff. New attention visualizations reuse these existing comparators; no retained comparison changes its method membership.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a dataset-substitution fine-tuning control in Section 5.5. The qualitative comparison also changes the stated sweater prompt from 'Purple woolen sweater' to 'Light purple woolen textile sweater'; this does not establish a rerun. Original training settings, metrics, test-set counts and evaluator counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially broadens the diagnostic evidence beyond the existing component and alpha ablations. It adds a control addressing dataset versus model contributions, attention analyses of attribute composition and component localization, and visual examples of previously acknowledged logo failures. Section 5.2 also reports checks involving unrecognized fabric names.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The 28-pair averaging procedure already appears in v1; its expanded supplementary description introduces no new uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Main benchmark and human/MLLM scores are unchanged. V2 Table 3 adds 'w/o MMDGarment' results: CLIPScore 0.7635, FID 9.4932 and LPIPS 0.6385, alongside new qualitative diagnostic examples. Section 5.3 revises stated FID/LPIPS improvements over IP-Adapter from 18.3%/9.9% to 20.3%/14.5%; the unchanged FID values actually imply approximately 20.14%, so these are reporting revisions, not improved model scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and assumptions remain the same, with no added proofs or theoretical results. Equation 2 replaces the undefined A_s with the preceding self-attention output f_s, a notation repair rather than a substantive change to the derivation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the FS2RG task, the MMDGarment dataset, a framework combining semantic enhancement with modality harmonization, and state-of-the-art performance. Additional explanations and supporting analyses do not materially change these central contributions.

C2.justification: V2 attributes gains primarily to its modules rather than dataset scale, interprets attention maps as supporting modality harmony, and expands claims about human/MLLM agreement and reliability. The design-stage evaluation boundary and tiny-logo limitation already existed in v1; they are relocated and illustrated in supplementary Section 10.

D1.justification: V1 promises future code/data release; v2 states availability and supplies a repository address. V2 also documents fabric-term normalization and fallback behavior, professional sketch provenance, and human questionnaire criteria and participant backgrounds. These expand reproducibility information while retaining the existing training hyperparameters and hardware details.

R1.justification: The bibliography retains the same 38 works and the related-work discussion is largely unchanged. V2's introduction adds an explicit contrast with T2I-Adapter and IP-Adapter concerning modality-conflict resolution, modestly sharpening its positioning against existing adapters.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted wording corrections, renames MSE to MMSE, fixes the unresolved ablation-table reference, and adds contribution and funding notes. Dataset and evaluation descriptions are shortened in the main text and expanded in supplementary sections, alongside relocated limitations. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds a retrieval diagram, dataset-example panels, attention visualizations and a failure-case figure. It redraws the framework more clearly, revises qualitative-comparison annotations to distinguish fabric and structural errors, and highlights table rankings. The dataset-comparison table moves to the supplement, and the author block and figure placement are substantially reformatted.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the study easier to assess through clearer retrieval and evaluation documentation, a concrete code/data access address, additional diagnostic evidence and illustrated limitations. The core results remain unchanged. Benefits are limited by the underspecified dataset control, its VITON-HD/VITON citation mismatch, and interpretations that exceed the demonstrated controls; the revised FID percentage also remains inconsistent with the table. Overall, transparency and presentation improve without resolving the main evidential limitations.
